title: Do both cities have long days in the same month?
description: The daylight per day of two cities is read across the year and compared with a full day of twenty four hours. The video finds the pattern of each city and which swings more. Keeko thinks both cities peak in June.
teaching_notes: One idea: read the whole year's pattern of a graph, not a single month, and compare daylight with a full day. Watch for students who think two cities share the same seasons.

source: Average daylight per day in two cities across the year: describe both patterns, compare the extremes, and compare June and December daylight with a full day of 24 hours
video_script.why: The child has found daylight per day and now reads the pattern of a whole year in two cities.
video_script.substitution: The book's own clustered bar graph of average daylight hours per day for City 1 and City 2.
video_script.anchor: Average daylight per day in hours. City 1: January 6.8, June 18.8, December 6. City 2: January 14.8, June 9.2, December 15.1.
video_script.wrong_move: Assumes both cities have summer at the same time, so both would have their longest days in June.
video_script.payoff_line: City one peaks in June and City two peaks in December.

final_answer.value: City 1 peaks in June and City 2 in December; City 1 swings more (12.8 hours against 5.9), because the cities lie in opposite hemispheres, far from the Equator
final_answer.spoken: City one peaks in June and City two in December; City one swings more, twelve point eight hours against five point nine

maths_rules: City 1: 6.8 in January, 18.8 in June (maximum), 6 in December (minimum)
City 2: 14.8 in January, 9.2 in June (minimum), 15.1 in December (maximum)
range of City 1: 18.8 - 6 = 12.8 hours; range of City 2: 15.1 - 9.2 = 5.9 hours; 12.8 > 5.9
a full day is 24 hours: 24 x 3 / 4 = 18, so 18.8 hours is about three quarters of a day
24 / 4 = 6, so 6 hours is about a quarter of a day
video_script.design: One idea: read a whole year's pattern, not one month. The six daylight readings sit in the anchor; on the board two lines trace each city through the year, and a 24 hour clock shows the part of the day that is daylight.
open_questions: The January daylight readings (6.8 and 14.8) come from the worklist; the extracted book text gives only the graph's described maxima and minima (about 17 to 18 and 6 hours for City 1, about 9 and 15 hours for City 2). Check against the printed graph.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, compare City one with a full day of twenty four hours.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>A quarter of twenty four is six.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>December daylight is about a quarter of the day.
